reading.body:
H.R. 6371, the No Robot Bosses Act, has 13 cosponsors and 6 lobbying filings naming it, with four of those filings from labor and civil liberties organizations.

The cosponsor list is almost entirely Democratic, with one Republican, James Moylan. The lobbying side is unions and rights groups: the AFL-CIO, the ACLU, the Communications Workers of America, and the National Treasury Employees Union. The bill's subject matter, automated decision systems in employment, explains that alignment. The organizations most likely to name it in filings are the ones whose members would be managed by such systems.

The data covers sponsorship, cosponsorship, and which organizations named the bill in lobbying filings. It does not include the text of the bill, any committee action, any vote, or the positions those organizations took. A filing naming a bill shows the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not support or opposition. The latest status date is 2025-12-03, and the filing count covers 2025 or later only.

Nothing here ties to compute, buildings, or power. This is labor and workplace governance, not infrastructure. The useful reading is narrow: who is behind the bill, and which organizations are paying attention to it.
